hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned a significant national recognition by being selected as one of only 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city stands alone as the only Florida municipality chosen for this prestigious honor this year. The award was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders presented their initiatives focused on strengthening community engagement and collaborative problem-solving.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the achievement, stating that "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He credited the award to the city's sustained commitment to revitalization and improving residents' quality of life. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson emphasized that the honor reflects the community itself. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

The All-America City Award recognizes communities that unite residents, government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and drive lasting improvements. Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs demonstrating its commitment to civic participation. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in leadership and advocacy work. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, maintains a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants enabling longtime homeowners to make essential repairs. Miller-Anderson emphasized the city's broader philosophy: "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city."

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders view this designation as validation of their progress while positioning Riviera Beach for future growth and opportunities. Miller-Anderson noted that the award "brings back community pride" and reinforces positive momentum. Officials believe the recognition signals to the nation that Riviera Beach represents a place where collaboration generates results and residents remain actively engaged in determining their community's direction. The nine other 2026 award recipients include Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for social media comments about political commentator Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended after labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi in Facebook comments. In the Thursday filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, stating that numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and removing him was appropriate.

Livingstone issued an order last month citing a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item projects, though he said he was not trying to set a record after vetoing a historic $3.1 billion in 2022. DeSantis said he cut items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions in road construction projects, teacher pay increases, and cancer research. It sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. DeSantis also rejected a $750 million transfer the Legislature wanted to make to the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund.

Among the cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged the Governor to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that it labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of the 621 appropriations the group wanted slashed.

DeSantis also indicated he will not formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed constitutional amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. He said he might participate if asked but would not spearhead efforts himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor due to term limits.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats staffed with medics patrolling north and south waterways as hundreds of boaters celebrate the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. The Martin County Maritime Response Unit will deploy two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county to assist boaters in need.

Lt. Brett Harry with the Maritime Response Unit said his team is prepared to help with injuries ranging from minor issues like stubbed toes to more serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Jay Collins' wife of running anti-Governor social media accounts
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous X accounts critical of Gov. Ron DeSantis were deactivated after prominent veterans of the Governor's communications team alleged they were tied to Second Lady Layla Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, identified multiple X accounts they alleged were operated by Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins. She stated the account content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor.

Redfern confirmed the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Juno Beach considers thousands in costs to replace fence at JB-7 beach access after resident complaints
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
A dispute over a missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point has created friction between condo residents and beachgoers, with potential solutions carrying a significant price tag for the town. Residents of the Colony Condos have complained that people accessing the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting across their private property since the town removed the fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now marking the boundary between the public path and private land, trespassers have easy access to the residential area.

Colony resident Lori Hill described the problem as especially severe during summer months. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill noted that when the fence was in place, residents had a clear boundary to point out to violators. Without it, confrontations have become routine, forcing residents to call police to address trespassers on their property.

Not all beachgoers see a problem. Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking area, said he has not witnessed the incidents residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said, adding that he has never seen anyone crossing the shrub line.

The issue was brought to the Juno Beach Town Council, where officials clarified the town is not legally required to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring lower-cost alternatives to a full fence replacement. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Hill expressed hope that the town would act on the concern. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," she said. The council decided to address the fence question during budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with S.D. Spady Elementary School making a dramatic leap from a C rating to an A.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district also achieved a record-setting 93.5 percent graduation rate, with 86 percent of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the biggest success stories came from Delray Beach, where S.D. Spady Elementary School jumped from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, said the school had an "A" rating two years ago and narrowly missed a "B" rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" rating to an "A" this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band earned a coveted spot in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will represent the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the moment, noting that millions, if not billions, of people will be watching. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion," Cabezas said. She explained the physical demands of marching band, saying, "You have to play, you have to breathe, you have to walk. Most people don't realize how difficult it is to walk and maintain that consistent sound without hearing the steps in your music."

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on execution. "Just focusing on the marching, the timing of everything. Everybody is going to be able to see it," Restivo said. "Everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of." Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying she has "full confidence in our students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and we'll rise to the occasion and represent our country well." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark and her surgeon are speaking out after Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that GalaFlex's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. "This product is giving my patients the least amount of complications, and other plastic surgeons as well," Billington said. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex a little more than a week ago. Anthem responded that the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy." Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial, and a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent this year as inflation hits holiday staples
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5 percent, while buns are up 7.7 percent. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4 percent. Ice cream prices have also climbed 5.3 percent compared to last year.

Not all items on the cookout menu have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or salad. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended several strategies to manage holiday meal costs. She emphasized shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for specific grocery items. Woroch also highlighted that cutting food waste is crucial for families, which begins with creating a meal plan before shopping.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Her fiancé Mark is now rebuilding his life after losing both his home and his future wife in the tragedy.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said. She later returned to the scene of the fire in the days following the tragedy to process her grief. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. "It's completely a state of devastation," Fenn said.

Fenn remembered White as a devoted Christian woman with many passions. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss carries additional weight for Mark, who has already experienced profound tragedy. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said.

The timing of White's death adds further heartbreak for those who knew her. "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said. Despite the devastating loss, Fenn said White's memory will remain with those close to her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said. The community continues to rally around Mark during this difficult time as he faces the dual grief of losing his fiancée and rebuilding his home.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city, accommodating both growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The widening project will also add bike and pedestrian paths and sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network linking West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The company describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, functioning like a "horizontal elevator" that bypasses traffic congestion entirely. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. The guideway would resemble a narrow pedestrian bridge, with stations potentially integrated into buildings to shield riders from South Florida heat and rain.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. Glydways currently operates a testing facility in California and has a project under construction near Atlanta's airport expected to begin offering rides by year's end.

He credited the award to the city's sustained commitment to revitalization and improving residents' quality of life. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson emphasized that the honor reflects the community itself. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

The All-America City Award recognizes communities that unite residents, government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and drive lasting improvements. Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs demonstrating its commitment to civic participation. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in leadership and advocacy work. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, maintains a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants enabling longtime homeowners to make essential repairs. Miller-Anderson emphasized the city's broader philosophy: "We're doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city."

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, ranks among the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders view this designation as validation of their progress while positioning Riviera Beach for future growth and opportunities. Miller-Anderson noted that the award "brings back community pride" and reinforces positive momentum. Officials believe the recognition signals to the nation that Riviera Beach represents a place where collaboration generates results and residents remain actively engaged in determining their community's direction. The nine other 2026 award recipients include Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan for Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike as part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the current entrances and exits to the Turnpike in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city, allowing the city to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike and improvements to the Turnpike bridge are still in the design phase. FDOT said the Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock to close Monday for $3 million renovation doubling slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation that will nearly double its capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and non-motor.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, the renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises will be allowed to build a gate at the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock to continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock plays a central role in the city's identity and economy. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and hopes the project will add more floating docks.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiance, Misty Dawn White, 46, in a deadly home fire earlier this week. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark, stating that Misty had passed away in the fire.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and people. She played the piano and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Adding to the heartbreak, White's birthday is the Fourth of July, meaning she passed just a few days before her birthday. Fenn said White will always be in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Glydways proposes elevated autonomous transit linking West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, potentially cutting the trip to under 10 minutes.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept is designed to function like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without getting stuck in traffic or making multiple intermediate stops.

Under the proposal, small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. While the company has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, reaching $73.82 for 10 people
cards.teaser: A holiday cookout meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5% and buns are up 7.7%.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a Fourth of July holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%, and ice cream prices are up 5.3%.

Not all food prices have increased this year. Potato prices are down, benefiting those planning to serve potato chips or salad. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide better pricing. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals. She emphasized that families should prioritize reducing food waste, which starts with creating a meal plan before shopping.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. After undergoing the mastectomy, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for her reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before the procedure was scheduled. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex surgical mesh was considered "investigational" with insufficient proof that it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that, while popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes insurance companies should reconsider their policies. Despite the denial, Clark underwent her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield stated the mesh does not currently meet coverage standards without FDA approval for breast reconstruction, though the company covers other evidence-based alternatives and has communicated with Clark's physician. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is aiming for a state championship this fall after finishing last season with a 10-2 record and capturing their district title. Despite the strong regular season, a second-round playoff loss has motivated the program to push harder toward deeper postseason success in 2026.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the strength of his senior class as a major advantage heading into the season. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. The veteran leadership from players who have progressed through the program's ranks since middle school provides a foundation of experience and continuity.

To prepare for a more competitive playoff run, the Scots have intentionally strengthened their schedule for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the tougher matchups, saying "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." This approach aims to both prepare the team for stronger opponents in the playoffs and draw recruits interested in competing against quality programs.

For the Scots, the ultimate measure of success this season centers on postseason advancement rather than the regular season record. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized this priority, noting "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters." The team is using their demanding summer training regimen as motivation for the work ahead. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described how the daily workouts provide purpose and direction, saying "It just adds up every day as something like to look forward to. Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record." With a veteran senior class leading the charge through intensive summer preparation, the Scots believe they have the pieces in place to transform their district success into a state championship run.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats staffed with medics patrolling north and south waterways as hundreds of boaters celebrate the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. The Martin County Maritime Response Unit will deploy two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county to assist boaters in need.

Lt. Brett Harry with the Maritime Response Unit said his team is prepared to help with injuries ranging from minor issues like stubbed toes to more serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, said safety is their top priority when taking their family on the water for the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman remembered by friends after dying in Monday home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a Hobe Sound home fire that investigators believe may have been caused by an electrical issue. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiancé Mark. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, who was friends with White for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, piano and children. White's birthday is July 4, meaning she died just days before turning 47. Fenn said White will always be remembered as a good soul who was the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Mark lost his only child Jacob in a separate tragedy.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes July 6 for $3 million renovation expanding to 44 slips
cards.teaser: The downtown Stuart public dock will close for a year of renovations funded by state grants, nearly doubling capacity from 18 to 44 slips for boaters.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses relying on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the non-floating section to board customers during construction, according to Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and expressed hope the project will add more floating docks.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court document Thursday arguing that reinstating Spectrum Academy teacher Matt Theobald would be inappropriate after his Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. In an order issued last month, Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, the only Florida city honored this year.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it one of just 10 communities in the U.S. selected for the honor and the only Florida city chosen this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver and recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." She added that winning the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof repaired after WPTV intervention
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home and unfinished roof repairs completed after WPTV contacted the roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. After making six payments totaling more than $17,000, McCoy said the company left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails beginning in January. He said he attempted to contact the company multiple times, including visiting their building in person two or three times, but received no meaningful response after a worker promised on Feb. 5 that the owner would call him.

The situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply sent letters warning that a nearly $7,000 lien had been filed against McCoy's property because Seabreeze Roofing had not paid for materials. McCoy turned to WPTV's Let's Hear It event in Boynton Beach for help. WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour of that conversation, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed and notarized by Gulfeagle Supply, lifting the lien from his property. The contractor also sent crews back to fix the two unfinished areas on his roof.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment.

The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups encourage beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this year's event also recognizes America's 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Jay Collins' wife of running anti-Governor social media accounts
hero.teaser: Multiple anonymous X accounts critical of Gov. Ron DeSantis were deactivated after prominent veterans of the Governor's communications team alleged they were tied to Second Lady Layla Collins.
hero.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, identified multiple X accounts they alleged were operated by Layla Collins, wife of Lt. Gov. Jay Collins. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to known contact information used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins. She stated the account content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor.

Redfern confirmed the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item projects, though he said he was not trying to set a record after vetoing a historic $3.1 billion in 2022. DeSantis said he cut items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions in road construction projects, teacher pay increases, and cancer research. It sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. DeSantis also rejected a $750 million transfer the Legislature wanted to make to the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund.

Among the cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged the Governor to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that it labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of the 621 appropriations the group wanted slashed.

DeSantis also indicated he will not formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed constitutional amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. He said he might participate if asked but would not spearhead efforts himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor due to term limits.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd seeks to keep Paula Stark off House District 47 ballot
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to reject Paula Stark's lawsuit seeking ballot access after she failed to submit required paperwork before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the House District 47 ballot, arguing she failed to properly file required paperwork. Stark submitted incomplete qualifying materials less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12. Five state employees gave sworn written court declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, nor was he accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork. Byrd contended that if Stark or Davis had questioned why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back or had not waited until the final hour, the mistake could have been discovered in time.

Three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6, according to Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve. Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve also cited Stark's history of campaign finance violations, noting Davis filed reports over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and maintains an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 would feature only Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves, representing a significant advantage for Democrats in the traditionally blue district covering Osceola and Orange counties.

cards.headline: Florida state parks waive admission fees for America's 250th Independence Day
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is offering free admission to state parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced that all residents and visitors can explore Florida state parks for free from July 3 through July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The free admission applies to day use only at most parks. All other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remain in effect. Three parks are excluded from the free admission: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park.

Florida's state parks offer hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding, as well as caverns, wetlands, beaches and springs. The parks also include historic sites such as forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other historic landmarks. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and family to enjoy the outdoors and support public lands during this significant moment in the nation's history. Information about parks is available at FloridaStateParks.org.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks and parades
cards.teaser: Fourth of July weekend brings fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities mark the semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Southwest Florida communities are celebrating America's 250th birthday across multiple locations this Fourth of July weekend. Sarasota's bayfront will host an America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m. Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch at 1560 Lakefront Drive in Sarasota will feature circus acts, carnival games, a kids zone, food and a drone show at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., with fireworks launching at dusk. The event is 100% funded by local residents, businesses and community supporters.

Additional celebrations include Longboat Key's Freedom Fest at Bicentennial Park, 2730 Gulf of Mexico Drive, featuring the "Shortest Parade in America," a rededication of Bicentennial Park and the Hot Diggity Dog costume contest. Historic Downtown Venice will hold a patriotic parade beginning at 9:30 a.m. at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques, with fireworks at the South Jetty scheduled to start between 9 and 9:15 p.m., with contingency plans to reschedule to July 5 if needed. Fort Myers Beach will kick off with a parade starting at 10 a.m. at Bay Oaks Recreation Center heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m. North Port's CoolToday Park will host Freedom Festival: Cheers to 250 Years from 6 to 9:30 p.m., with fireworks scheduled for 9 p.m.

cards.headline: Delray Beach celebrates America's 250th with time capsule opening and beach festivities
cards.teaser: Delray Beach's Fourth of July celebration will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule and host fireworks as an official America250 partner event.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition spanning more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people, is an official America250 partner event marking the nation's 250th anniversary. At 5 p.m. on the Main Stage at A1A, the city will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule containing a message from Americans who celebrated the nation's 200th birthday. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag rises at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

Beach activities begin at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, a sand-sculpting competition presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs. Judging occurs at 11 a.m. with a requirement to keep creations patriotic, not political. From noon to 1 p.m., guided snorkel and scuba tours explore the S.S. Inchulva, a British steamship torn apart by a 1903 hurricane 150 yards offshore, known as the Delray Wreck. Evening entertainment features Let's Groove Tonight and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display launches at 9 p.m. Roads close from noon to 11 p.m. The city urges visitors to park west of the Intracoastal Bridge, with free FreeBee rides available downtown.

cards.headline: Ocala and Marion County stage four synchronized fireworks displays for semiquincentennial
cards.teaser: Marion County will launch synchronized fireworks displays at four locations to celebrate America's 250th anniversary under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four sites on July 4, each beginning at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks light up the sky at 9 p.m. The locations are Veterans Memorial Park at 2601 E. Fort King St. in Ocala, Wrigley Fields at 405 E. Highway 316 in Citra, Dunnellon High School at 10055 SW 180th Ave. Rd. in Dunnellon, and the Belleview Sportsplex at 6501 SE 107th St. in Belleview. The celebration marks the semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, being commemorated nationwide through America250, the nonpartisan initiative of the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission.

The city of Ocala hosts Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration with live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Ocala-based country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities. The Patriot Parade kicks off at Southeast 16th Avenue, heads up to Silver Springs Boulevard and wraps up near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening.

hero.headline: Martin County maritime medics deploy two boats for Fourth of July weekend
hero.teaser: The Martin County Maritime Response Unit has two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters celebrate the holiday weekend.
hero.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will deploy two boats with medics on standby in north and south Martin County to respond to emergencies ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched Friday from the ramps at Sandsprit Park in Martin County with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate suspended teacher
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a Thursday court challenge against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectru.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a Thursday court challenge against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy who was suspended last year for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk. The board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made findings not based on competent substantial evidence when she recommended Theobald be reinstated with back pay and benefits. The board's attorney contends the Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and that removing Theobald was appropriate.

Theobald, who has taught at Spectrum Academy since 2009, made comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: Costco is planning its first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
The warehouse retailer is planning to open its first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie. The store would be the first Costco location serving St. Lucie County and the broader Treasure Coast region, giving local residents access to Costco's warehouse shopping without traveling to other counties.

No specific timeline or location details for the Port St. Lucie Costco have been disclosed. However, the planned store comes as Port St. Lucie pursues major infrastructure improvements to support the city's continued growth. The city is currently working on expanding Midway Road and adding a partial interchange to the Florida Turnpike, projects designed to improve accessibility and reduce congestion in the area.

Port St. Lucie City Council recently approved the first reading of an ordinance to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to help facilitate the Turnpike interchange. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange addresses an important gap in the current system. "There's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie," Samples said. He emphasized that the interchange is about keeping up with the city's expansion. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is advancing to support this growth. Crews are currently working on the first phase, which widens the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing the partial interchange, which is still in the design phase. The Midway Road project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to improve safety and accessibility. City council will vote on final approval to donate the land at an upcoming meeting.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
hero.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
The Fourth of July tradition of cookouts, grilling and picnics comes with a higher price tag this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the driver behind increased costs. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically to keep costs in check. She said families should compare stores to see who has the best deals for groceries on their list and cut down food waste by beginning with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the Florida Department of Education. School districts and schools receive letter grades based on several factors, including student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, were rated A or B, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, and 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework by taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the biggest success stories came from Delray Beach, where S.D. Spady Elementary School made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year. Leading the turnaround effort is Principal Rona Tata, who has spent the last 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal. Tata said the school had an A rating two years ago but narrowly missed a B rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a C rating to an A this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. City leaders say the recognition reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and local government, and creating opportunities for the community to play a direct role in shaping the city's future.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents want fence back at JB-7 beach access point
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer, with visitors parking in private spots and pushing back bushes to access the beach with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said residents remember when the fence made the boundary clear, and since it came down, confrontations with trespassers have become a recurring problem. Residents have escalated to calling police to address the issues.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting a combination of split rail fencing and shrubs. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. Not all beachgoers agree a problem exists. Michael House, a visitor to JB-7, said he has not witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football eyes state title run after 10-2 season
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with their sights set on a state title. After finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, the team's second-round playoff exit has motivated them to pursue bigger goals. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players who came from the middle school and understand how the program operates. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run," Robertson said.

With a veteran senior class leading the way, the Scots are scheduling more challenging opponents this fall to elevate their competition level. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the tougher schedule, saying the team wanted to take their program to the next level by playing against really good teams. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that playoff advancement matters more than a perfect regular season record. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean noted that summer workouts provide daily motivation as the team prepares for the season ahead.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient and surgeon speak out after insurance denial
cards.teaser: A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considers "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, believes insurance companies should reconsider their stance. She uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem responded by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, but added that without FDA approval, the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy."
